headline: Some investors are reportedly weighing a lower valuation of about $1.5 trillion for Anthropic's planned stock market debut, down from roughly $2 trillion, after its revenue growth slowed.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a possible 25% cut to the price of the biggest AI lab listing is big, but it rests on four unnamed sources and is not a final price.
importance_line: Matters to investors, retirement funds and other buyers of the planned shares, and is an early test of appetite for AI listings; the valuation talk comes from four unnamed sources and no price has been set.
summary: Reuters reports, citing four people familiar with the matter and as relayed by Stocktwits, that some investors are considering a valuation near $1.5 trillion for Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI assistant, down from the roughly $2 trillion expected earlier. This follows revenue figures given to investors on 14 Oct 2026, reported by Bloomberg and others as $16.8 billion for the third quarter, up 45% on the second quarter after a 147% jump the quarter before; Anthropic has not confirmed those figures.
notes: Reuters article not opened (blocked); text read via Stocktwits, which credits Reuters. Continues the revenue story of the 15 Oct pool; new today is the valuation reassessment.
